definition_zh: 每件事；一切；最重要的事
definition_en: all things
core_image: 搬家时堆满房间的纸箱，标签写满各种物品名

sceneCN: 这里 everything 是「一切事物」（第 1 个义项：某一情境中的所有事物）；句意：搬家那天，屋里的一切都被装进纸箱。

pos.zh: 每件事；一切；最重要的事

senses.title: All things
senses.definition: all things in a situation
senses.definitionCN: 某一情境中的所有事物
senses.example: Everything in the room was new.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里的一切都是新的。
senses.why: Every and thing join to cover all objects.

senses.title: All that matters
senses.definition: the thing of greatest importance

senses.exampleCN: 家人对她来说就是一切。
senses.why: The word can carry emotional weight beyond objects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能承载超出物品的情感重量。

senses.title: All details
senses.definition: all the details of a matter
senses.example: Tell me everything about the trip.

intro.en: Everything joins every to thing, an old word for an object or matter.
intro.cn: everything 由 every 与 thing（古义为物品或事情）组合而成。

items.en: Thing means an object or matter.
items.cn: thing 意为物品或事情。

items.en: Every means each member of a set.
items.cn: every 意为集合中的每一个。

items.en: Every plus thing forms everything.
items.cn: every 加 thing 构成 everything。

items.en: It means all objects in a situation.
items.cn: 它指某一情境中的所有物品。

items.en: It can also mean what matters most.
items.cn: 它也可以指最重要的事。

note.en: Everything covers all things; something is one unknown thing.
note.cn: everything 涵盖所有事物；something 指某件未知的事。

normalIntro.en: Everything is every thing packed into one word.

normal.en: Everything in order means all is ready.
normal.cn: everything in order 意为一切就绪。

normal.en: Tell me everything means tell all details.

normal.en: Compare nothing: everything is all, nothing is none.

abstract.en: Think of a word that leaves nothing outside it.

examples.en: Everything was ready before the guests arrived.

definition_en: in every place

senses.title: In all places
senses.definition: in every place

senses.why: Total place can shade into wide spread.
senses.whyCN: 地点的全部可以引申为广泛的传播。

items.en: Hwǣr means where.

definition_en: facts or signs that show something is true
core_image: 桌上摆着放大镜、照片和一叠文件

senses.title: A sign
senses.definition: a sign that something is true
senses.example: There is evidence of rain in the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 山里有下雨的迹象。
senses.why: The word extends from courts to ordinary observation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法庭延伸到日常观察。

senses.title: To show
senses.definition: to show or prove something
senses.example: The results evidence a clear improvement.
senses.exampleCN: 结果显示出明显的改善。
senses.why: The noun also became a formal verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也变成了正式动词。

intro.cn: evidence 源自拉丁语 evidentia（清楚），来自 evidens（清楚可见的）。

items.en: Videre means to see.

items.en: Evidentia means clearness.

abstract.en: Think of a light that makes a hidden fact visible.

examples.en: The evidence supports her story.
examples.cn: 证据支持她的说法。

examples.en: Scientists found evidence of water on the planet.
examples.cn: 科学家在这颗行星上发现了水的证据。

examples.en: He gave evidence in court.
examples.cn: 他在法庭上作证。

root: 拉丁语 evidentia（清楚可见）← evidens（显露的）← e-（出）＋ videre（看）→ evidence。

sensesIntro.en: Evidence begins as proof in a case, extends to any sign, and then becomes a formal verb meaning to show.
sensesIntro.cn: evidence 先指案件中的证据，再指任何迹象，最后作正式动词表示表明。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnifying glass, photos and papers on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的放大镜、照片与文件。

branches.en: Proof in a case is the core sense.
branches.cn: 案件中的证据是核心含义。

branches.en: Any sign can count as evidence.
branches.cn: 任何迹象都可算作证据。

branches.en: The verb means to show clearly.
branches.cn: 动词意为清楚地表明。

branches.en: Courts and daily life both read signs.
branches.cn: 法庭与日常生活都在解读迹象。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one act of showing.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共用一个展示行为。

intro.en: Evidence comes from the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: evidence 来自拉丁词根 vid（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin evidentia gives the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evidentia 赋予这个词形态。

items.exampleCN: evidens 由 e- 与 videre 组成。
evident 描述清楚明显的事物。

definition_en: easy to see or understand
core_image: 雨后的路上清晰的一串脚印
scene: 雨停后，泥地上的一串脚印清楚地说明有人来过。After the rain stopped, a line of footprints in the mud made it evident that someone had been there.
sceneCN: 这里 evident 是「明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易看清或理解）；句意：雨停后，泥地上的一串脚印清楚地说明有人来过。

senses.title: Easy to see
senses.definition: easy to see or notice
senses.example: The damage was evident at once.
senses.exampleCN: 损坏立刻就看出来了。
senses.why: Evident descends from Latin evidens, clearly seen.
senses.whyCN: evident 源自拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的）。

senses.title: Easy to understand
senses.definition: clear to the mind
senses.example: It was evident that she was tired.
senses.exampleCN: 她显然累了。
senses.why: What is clear to the eye becomes clear to thought.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛看得清楚的事也变成思想上的明白。

senses.title: An obvious judgment
senses.definition: used to state a clear fact
senses.example: His answer was evident to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答对所有人来说都明摆着。
senses.why: The adjective often introduces an obvious judgment.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词常引出明显的判断。

intro.en: Evident comes from Latin evidens, clearly seen, from videre, to see.
intro.cn: evident 源自拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的），来自 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre means to see.
items.cn: videre 意为看。

items.en: Evidens means clearly seen.
items.cn: evidens 意为清楚可见的。

items.en: French evident keeps the sense of clear.
items.cn: 法语 evident 保留了清楚的含义。

items.en: Evident describes what is easy to see.
items.cn: evident 描述容易看见的事物。

items.en: It also describes what is easy to understand.
items.cn: 它也描述容易理解的事物。

note.en: Evident stresses what the facts show; obvious stresses what no one can miss.
note.cn: evident 强调事实显示出来的清楚；obvious 强调谁都不会错过。

normalIntro.en: Evident is a fact standing in plain sight.
normalIntro.cn: evident 是摆在明处的事实。

normal.en: Evident from the photo means the photo shows it.
normal.cn: evident from the photo 意为照片上看得出来。

normal.en: Clearly evident means very easy to see.
normal.cn: clearly evident 意为非常明显。

normal.en: Evident to all means everyone can see it.
normal.cn: evident to all 意为所有人都看得出来。

normal.en: Make it evident means show it clearly.
normal.cn: make it evident 意为把它清楚地显示出来。

normal.en: Compare obvious: evident comes from what is seen, obvious from what blocks the way.
normal.cn: 对比 obvious：evident 强调看见，obvious 强调挡在眼前无法忽视。

abstract.en: Picture clear footprints after rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后清晰的脚印。

abstract.en: Imagine a fact written in letters large enough to read from afar.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用远处也能看清的大字写出的事实。

abstract.en: Think of a curtain pulled back from a bright window.
abstract.cn: 想象明亮的窗帘被拉开。

examples.en: The reason for the delay was evident.
examples.cn: 延误的原因很明显。

examples.en: It was evident from her face that she had cried.
examples.cn: 从她脸上明显看得出她哭过。

examples.en: The improvement is evident in every chapter.
examples.cn: 每一章都能看出改进。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ vident（看见）」——一眼就能看见，就是明显的。

root: 拉丁语 evidens（清楚可见的）← e-（出）＋ videre（看）→ evident，核心义「看得出来的」。

sensesIntro.en: Evident begins with what is easy to see, extends to what is easy to understand, and often states an obvious judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: evident 从容易看见开始，延伸到容易理解，也常用来陈述明显的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clear footprints left on a path after rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨后小路上清晰的脚印。

branches.en: What is easy to see comes first.
branches.cn: 容易看见是首要含义。

branches.en: What is easy to understand follows.
branches.cn: 容易理解紧随其后。

branches.en: The word often states an obvious fact.
branches.cn: 这个词常陈述明显事实。

branches.en: Sight and understanding share one clarity.
branches.cn: 看见与理解共享同一种清楚。

branches.en: A visible fact becomes an obvious judgment.
branches.cn: 可见事实变成明显判断。

intro.en: Evident comes from the Latin root vid, to see.
intro.cn: evident 来自拉丁词根 vid（看）。

latinIntro.en: Latin evidens is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evidens 是直接来源。

definition_en: in a way that is easy to see or understand
core_image: 没关的灯和湿伞，说明有人刚回来
scene: 灯还亮着，湿伞靠在门边，显然他刚回来。The lamp was still on and a wet umbrella leaned by the door, so evidently he had just come back.
sceneCN: 这里 evidently 是「显然」（第 1 个义项：根据可见迹象判断）；句意：灯还亮着，湿伞靠在门边，显然他刚回来。

senses.title: Clearly
senses.definition: in a clear way
senses.example: She was evidently pleased with the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她显然对结果很满意。
senses.why: The adverb marks what is clear from the facts.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词标记从事实中看出的清楚结论。

senses.title: As shown by signs
senses.definition: according to what can be seen
senses.example: Evidently, the window was left open.
senses.exampleCN: 看样子窗户一直开着。
senses.why: The word often begins a conclusion drawn from signs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常引出从迹象得出的结论。

senses.title: Obvious to all
senses.definition: used when something is obvious
senses.example: He was evidently the leader of the group.
senses.exampleCN: 他显然是这群人的领头人。
senses.why: It can soften a judgment by pointing to clear signs.
senses.whyCN: 它通过指向明显迹象来缓和判断。

intro.en: Evidently is evident plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: evidently 是 evident 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Evidens means clearly seen.
items.cn: evidens 意为清楚可见的。

items.en: Evident describes what is clear.
items.cn: evident 描述清楚的事物。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: Evidently marks a clear conclusion.
items.cn: evidently 标记清楚的结论。

items.en: It often opens a sentence based on signs.
items.cn: 它常引出基于迹象的判断句。

note.en: Evidently points to clear signs; apparently leaves room for doubt.
note.cn: evidently 指向清楚迹象；apparently 留有余地。

entries.definition: as it seems from what is known
in an easy to understand way

normalIntro.en: Evidently is the word for a conclusion you can almost see.
normalIntro.cn: evidently 是几乎看得见的结论所用的词。

normal.en: Evidently true means clearly true.
normal.cn: evidently true 意为显然属实。

normal.en: Evidently pleased means clearly happy.
normal.cn: evidently pleased 意为显然高兴。

normal.en: Evidently wrong means clearly mistaken.
normal.cn: evidently wrong 意为显然错了。

normal.en: Quite evidently means very obviously.
normal.cn: quite evidently 意为十分明显。

normal.en: Compare apparently: apparently reports how things seem, evidently points to signs.
normal.cn: 对比 apparently：apparently 说看起来如何，evidently 指向迹象。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp left on and a wet umbrella by the door.
abstract.cn: 想象亮着的灯和门边的湿伞。

abstract.en: Imagine reading a story from the smallest clues.
abstract.cn: 想象从最小的线索读出整个故事。

abstract.en: Think of a sign that needs no explanation.
abstract.cn: 想象一个无需解释的标记。

examples.en: He was evidently nervous before the speech.
examples.cn: 演讲前他显然很紧张。

examples.en: Evidently, the message never arrived.
examples.cn: 看来那条消息从未送到。

examples.en: The team was evidently stronger than last year.
examples.cn: 这支队伍显然比去年更强。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evident（明显的）＋ ly」——以明显的方式，就是显然。

root: evident（明显的）＋ -ly（副词后缀）→ evidently，核心义「以看得出来的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: Evidently marks what is clear, draws a conclusion from signs, and can soften an obvious judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: evidently 标记清楚之事，从迹象得出结论，也能缓和明显的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp still on and a wet umbrella at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：亮着的灯与门边的湿伞。

branches.en: Clearness is the core meaning.
branches.cn: 清楚是核心含义。

branches.en: Signs lead to a conclusion.
branches.cn: 迹象引出结论。

branches.en: The word can mark an obvious judgment.
branches.cn: 这个词能标记明显的判断。

branches.en: What is clear is often read from signs.
branches.cn: 清楚之事常从迹象读出。

branches.en: A clear fact becomes an obvious statement.
branches.cn: 清楚事实变成明显陈述。

intro.en: Evidently is evident plus -ly.
intro.cn: evidently 是 evident 加 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The base comes from Latin evidens.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词来自拉丁语 evidens。

items.example: Videre gives the root of seeing.

latinEntries.example: Evidens passes into English as evident.
latinEntries.exampleCN: evidens 进入英语成为 evident。

definition_en: morally bad or harmful
core_image: 阴影里伸出的手，抓住一束光
scene: 故事里的巫师用邪恶的咒语夺走了村庄的光。The wizard in the story used an evil spell to take away the light of the village.
sceneCN: 这里 evil 是「邪恶的」（第 1 个义项：道德上错误且残忍）；句意：故事里的巫师用邪恶的咒语夺走了村庄的光。

senses.title: Morally bad
senses.definition: morally wrong and cruel
senses.example: The evil king was feared by all.
senses.exampleCN: 所有人都惧怕那个邪恶的国王。
senses.why: The oldest sense is what harms others by choice.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是故意伤害他人。

senses.title: A great wrong
senses.definition: a very bad act or force
senses.example: They fought against evil in the world.
senses.exampleCN: 他们与世间的罪恶作斗争。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the force itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成指这种力量的名词。

senses.title: A harmful thing
senses.definition: something that causes great harm
senses.example: Greed is an evil that spreads quietly.
senses.exampleCN: 贪婪是一种悄然蔓延的祸害。
senses.why: Any great harm can be named an evil.
senses.whyCN: 任何巨大危害都可称为祸害。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word, yfel, shared by Germanic languages.
intro.cn: evil 是古英语词 yfel，在日耳曼语族中通用。

items.en: Yfel means bad or harmful.
items.cn: yfel 意为坏的或有害的。

items.en: The word is common to Germanic languages.
items.cn: 这个词在日耳曼语族中普遍存在。

items.en: Evil keeps the sense of moral harm.
items.cn: evil 保留了道德伤害的含义。

items.en: It also names the force of wrong.
items.cn: 它也指恶的力量。

items.en: Any great harm can be called an evil.
items.cn: 任何巨大危害都能称为祸害。

note.en: Evil implies deep moral wrong; bad is the general opposite of good.
note.cn: evil 指深刻的道德错误；bad 是 good 的通用反义词。

normalIntro.en: Evil is a shadow that chooses to swallow light.
normalIntro.cn: evil 是选择吞掉光明的阴影。

normal.en: An evil plan intends to hurt others.
normal.cn: an evil plan 意图伤害他人。

normal.en: Good and evil are old opposites.
normal.cn: good and evil 是古老的对照。

normal.en: An evil spirit is a harmful force.
normal.cn: an evil spirit 是害人的力量。

normal.en: The root of evil means the source of wrong.
normal.cn: the root of evil 意为罪恶的根源。

normal.en: Compare wicked: wicked stresses cruelty, evil stresses deep wrong.
normal.cn: 对比 wicked：wicked 强调残忍，evil 强调深刻的错误。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一只影子般的手穿过一束光。

abstract.en: Imagine a sweet voice that hides a sharp edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一个甜美却暗藏锋刃的声音。

abstract.en: Think of a door that opens into a very cold room.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇通向极冷房间的门。

examples.en: The story is about the battle between good and evil.
examples.cn: 这个故事讲的是善与恶的斗争。

examples.en: He had an evil plan.
examples.cn: 他有一个邪恶的计划。

examples.en: The medicine left an evil taste.
examples.cn: 这药留下了一股难闻的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「evil」倒过来是「live」——把生活颠倒，就成了 evil；这只是字母游戏，非词源。

root: 古英语 yfel（坏的）→ 中古英语 evel → evil，核心义「故意为害的」。

sensesIntro.en: Evil begins as moral badness, becomes the force of wrong, and then any great harm.
sensesIntro.cn: evil 从道德败坏开始，变成恶的力量，再指任何巨大危害。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand of shadow reaching through a beam of light.
core.cn: 核心意象：影子般的手穿过一束光。

branches.en: Moral badness is the core sense.
branches.cn: 道德败坏是核心含义。

branches.en: The force of wrong becomes a noun.
branches.cn: 恶的力量成为名词。

branches.en: Any great harm can be an evil.
branches.cn: 任何巨大危害都可是祸害。

branches.en: A bad act and a bad force share one word.
branches.cn: 恶行与恶的力量共用一个词。

branches.en: Cruelty and harm are both part of evil.
branches.cn: 残忍与伤害都属于恶。

intro.en: Evil is an old English word with a Germanic root.
intro.cn: evil 是带日耳曼词根的古英语词。

latinIntro.en: It has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语来源。

items.example: Yfel is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: yfel 是现存最古老的形式。
doer 出现在 evildoer 中。

definition_en: a slow process of change and development
core_image: 一条从鱼到鸟再到人的细线图
scene: 化石记录展示了鸟类翅膀在漫长岁月中的演变。The fossil record shows the evolution of bird wings over a very long time.
sceneCN: 这里 evolution 是「演变、进化」（第 1 个义项：缓慢变化发展的过程）；句意：化石记录展示了鸟类翅膀在漫长岁月中的演变。

senses.title: Biological change
senses.definition: the slow change of living things over generations
senses.definitionCN: 生物经过许多世代发生的缓慢变化
senses.example: Evolution explains how species adapt.
senses.exampleCN: 进化论解释了物种如何适应环境。
senses.why: The Latin root volvere means to roll, and unfolding is a kind of rolling out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 volvere 意为滚，展开就是滚开。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.definition: a slow change in ideas or systems
senses.definitionCN: 思想或制度的缓慢变化
senses.example: The evolution of language never stops.
senses.exampleCN: 语言的演变从未停止。
senses.why: The word extends from species to anything that develops.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从物种延伸到任何发展中的事物。

senses.title: An unfolding movement
senses.definition: a planned movement of troops or ships
senses.definitionCN: 部队或舰船的有计划移动
senses.example: The general ordered a careful evolution of the fleet.
senses.exampleCN: 将军命令舰队谨慎变换队形。
senses.why: The oldest sense is an unfolding or unrolling.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是展开或铺开。

intro.en: Evolution comes from Latin evolutio, an unrolling, from evolvere.
intro.cn: evolution 源自拉丁语 evolutio（展开），来自 evolvere。

items.en: Volvere means to roll.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚。

items.en: Evolvere means to roll out or unroll.
items.cn: evolvere 意为滚出或展开。

items.en: Evolutio names an unrolling.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开。

items.en: Evolution first names an unfolding movement.
items.cn: evolution 最初指展开的动作。

items.en: It comes to mean the slow change of species.
items.cn: 它逐渐指物种的缓慢变化。

note.en: Evolution is gradual change; revolution is a sudden complete turn.
note.cn: evolution 是渐进变化；revolution 是突然的彻底翻转。

entries.definition: to change slowly into a new form
the process of growing or changing

normalIntro.en: Evolution is a long scroll slowly unrolling through time.
normalIntro.cn: evolution 是随时间缓缓展开的长卷。

normal.en: The theory of evolution explains species change.
normal.cn: 进化论解释物种变化。

normal.en: Human evolution took millions of years.
normal.cn: 人类进化历经数百万年。

normal.en: The evolution of language is easy to see.
normal.cn: 语言的演变很容易看出来。

normal.en: Gradual evolution means slow change.
normal.cn: gradual evolution 意为缓慢变化。

normal.en: Compare revolution: evolution unfolds, revolution overturns.
normal.cn: 对比 revolution：evolution 展开，revolution 推翻。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line changing from fish to bird to human.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细线从鱼变到鸟再变到人。

abstract.en: Imagine a scroll unrolling one small picture at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象长卷一次展开一幅小图。

abstract.en: Think of a path that changes shape as it goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条边走边改变形状的路。

examples.en: Evolution takes place over many generations.
examples.cn: 进化经过许多世代才发生。

examples.en: The book traces the evolution of the bicycle.
examples.cn: 这本书追溯了自行车的演变。

examples.en: Scientists study the evolution of bird wings.
examples.cn: 科学家研究鸟类翅膀的进化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ volution（转）」——慢慢转出来、展开来，就是进化与演变。

root: 拉丁语 evolvere（展开）＝ e-（出）＋ volvere（滚）→ evolutio → evolution，核心义「逐渐展开」。

sensesIntro.en: Evolution starts as an unrolling, becomes biological change, and also names gradual development in any field.
sensesIntro.cn: evolution 从展开开始，成为生物变化，也指任何领域的逐渐发展。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line changing from fish to bird to human.
core.cn: 核心意象：从鱼到鸟再到人的细线。

branches.en: Biological change is the main modern sense.
branches.cn: 生物变化是现代主要含义。

branches.en: Any system can slowly evolve.
branches.cn: 任何体系都能缓慢演变。

branches.en: The old sense is an unfolding movement.
branches.cn: 古老含义是展开的动作。

branches.en: Species and languages both unfold over time.
branches.cn: 物种与语言都随时间展开。

branches.en: The unrolling image underlies both meanings.
branches.cn: 展开的意象支撑两种含义。

intro.en: Evolution combines e-, out, the root volv, to roll, and the suffix -ion.
intro.cn: evolution 由 e-（出）、词根 volv（滚）与后缀 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin evolvere and evolutio give the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evolvere 与 evolutio 赋予这个词形态。

definition_en: to change slowly into a new form
core_image: 一颗种子在四季里长成开花的树
scene: 这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。The plant evolved thicker leaves in order to survive the drought.
sceneCN: 这里 evolve 是「逐渐演化」（第 1 个义项：生物经过世代发展出新特征）；句意：这株植物为了适应干旱，逐渐演化出更厚的叶片。

senses.title: Biological change
senses.definition: to develop new features over generations
senses.definitionCN: 经过许多世代发展出新特征
senses.example: Birds evolved from small dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类由小型恐龙进化而来。
senses.why: Evolvere means to unroll, as a species unfolds over time.
senses.whyCN: evolvere 意为展开，物种随时间展开。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.definition: to develop slowly
senses.example: The plan evolved into a full project.
senses.exampleCN: 计划逐渐发展成一个完整项目。
senses.why: Any idea can unfold like a living form.
senses.whyCN: 任何想法都能像生命形态一样展开。

senses.title: To give off
senses.definition: to give off gas or heat
senses.example: The reaction evolved a sharp smell.
senses.exampleCN: 反应释放出刺鼻的气味。
senses.why: Unrolling can mean letting something out.
senses.whyCN: 展开也可以指让某物释放出来。

intro.en: Evolve comes from Latin evolvere, to unroll.
intro.cn: evolve 源自拉丁语 evolvere（展开）。

items.en: Volvere means to roll.
items.cn: volvere 意为滚。

items.en: Evolvere means to unroll.
items.cn: evolvere 意为展开。

items.en: Evolve first means to unfold.
items.cn: evolve 最初指展开。

items.en: It comes to mean slow biological change.
items.cn: 它逐渐指缓慢的生物变化。

items.en: It also means to develop gradually.
items.cn: 它也指逐渐发展。

note.en: Evolve is slow and natural; develop can be planned.
note.cn: evolve 是缓慢自然的；develop 可以是有计划的。

entries.definition: to grow or change over time
to change to fit a new situation
to move toward a better state

normalIntro.en: Evolve is a seed slowly becoming a tree.
normalIntro.cn: evolve 是一颗种子慢慢长成树。

normal.en: Evolve from means come from an older form.
normal.cn: evolve from 意为从更早的形态发展而来。

normal.en: Evolve into means become something new.
normal.cn: evolve into 意为演变成新事物。

normal.en: Slowly evolve means change over a long time.
normal.cn: slowly evolve 意为经过很长时间变化。

normal.en: Evolve over time means develop gradually.
normal.cn: evolve over time 意为随时间逐渐发展。

normal.en: Compare develop: develop can be planned, evolve is usually natural.
normal.cn: 对比 develop：develop 可以计划，evolve 通常自然发生。

abstract.en: Picture a seed becoming a flowering tree through four seasons.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗种子在四季中长成开花的树。

abstract.en: Imagine a rough sketch slowly turning into a clear map.
abstract.cn: 想象粗糙草图慢慢变成清晰地图。

abstract.en: Think of a river that slowly finds a new path.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河慢慢找到新的河道。

examples.en: The company evolved from a small shop.
examples.cn: 这家公司由一家小店发展而来。

examples.en: Animals evolve to survive in new places.
examples.cn: 动物进化以适应新环境。

examples.en: Her style evolved over many years.
examples.cn: 她的风格经过许多年逐渐演变。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋ volve（转）」——慢慢转出来、展开来，就是进化、发展。

root: 拉丁语 evolvere（展开）＝ e-（出）＋ volvere（滚）→ evolve，核心义「逐渐展开、演化」。

sensesIntro.en: Evolve begins with biological change, extends to gradual development, and keeps an older sense of giving off.
sensesIntro.cn: evolve 从生物变化开始，延伸到逐渐发展，还保留了释放的旧义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed becoming a flowering tree through four seasons.
core.cn: 核心意象：种子在四季中长成开花的树。

branches.en: Species change is the core modern sense.
branches.cn: 物种变化是现代核心含义。

branches.en: Plans and styles can evolve too.
branches.cn: 计划与风格也能逐渐发展。

branches.en: The old sense is to give off.
branches.cn: 古老含义是释放。

branches.en: Nature and human plans both unfold.
branches.cn: 自然与人类计划都会展开。

branches.en: Unrolling underlies change and release.
branches.cn: 展开的意象支撑变化与释放。

intro.en: Evolve combines e-, out, with the Latin root volv, to roll.
intro.cn: evolve 由 e-（出）与拉丁词根 volv（滚）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin evolvere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 evolvere 是直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Evolvere is the direct Latin source.
latinEntries.exampleCN: evolvere 是直接拉丁语来源。

definition_en: a former partner, or a prefix meaning former
core_image: 旧相册里被剪掉一半的合影
scene: 谈到过去的婚姻时，他只说了一句「她是我的前任」。When talking about his past marriage, he only said that she was his ex.
sceneCN: 这里 ex 是「前任」（第 1 个义项：过去的伴侣）；句意：谈到过去的婚姻时，他只说了一句「她是我的前任」。

senses.title: Former partner
senses.definition: a former husband, wife, or partner
senses.definitionCN: 以前的丈夫、妻子或伴侣
senses.example: He is still friends with his ex.
senses.exampleCN: 他和前任仍然是朋友。
senses.why: The prefix ex- means out or former, and stands alone in speech.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 ex- 意为出或以前，在口语中可单独使用。

senses.title: Former
senses.definition: a prefix meaning former
senses.example: Her ex-husband lives abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她的前夫住在国外。
senses.why: The prefix attaches to titles and relations.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀附着在称谓和关系词前。

senses.title: Example abbreviation
senses.definition: a written short form of example
senses.example: See ex. 3 on the next page.
senses.exampleCN: 见下一页的例 3。
senses.why: Dictionaries shorten example to ex. in cross-references.
senses.whyCN: 词典在交叉引用中把 example 缩写成 ex.。

intro.en: Ex comes from the Latin preposition ex, meaning out of.
intro.cn: ex 来自拉丁语介词 ex（出自、向外）。

items.en: Ex means out of.
items.cn: ex 意为出自、向外。

items.en: The prefix ex- marks former status.
items.cn: 前缀 ex- 标记以前的身份。

items.en: Ex- appears in ex-wife and ex-king.
items.cn: ex- 出现在 ex-wife 与 ex-king 中。

items.en: Ex stands alone as a noun for a former partner.
items.cn: ex 可单独作名词，指前任。

items.en: The abbreviation ex. also shortens example.
items.cn: 缩写 ex. 也用来缩短 example。

note.en: Ex as a noun names a former partner; the prefix ex- marks former status.
note.cn: ex 作名词指前任；前缀 ex- 标记以前的身份。

entries.definition: a person one is close to

normalIntro.en: Ex is the small word for someone now outside your life.
normalIntro.cn: ex 是那个现在已经不在你生活里的人的小词。

normal.en: His ex means his former partner.
normal.cn: his ex 意为他的前任。

normal.en: Ex-wife means a former wife.
normal.cn: ex-wife 意为前妻。

normal.en: Ex-husband means a former husband.
normal.cn: ex-husband 意为前夫。

normal.en: Ex-boyfriend means a former boyfriend.
normal.cn: ex-boyfriend 意为前男友。

normal.en: Compare former: ex- is a prefix, former is a full adjective.
normal.cn: 对比 former：ex- 是前缀，former 是完整形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a photo cut in half, leaving one person.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被剪掉一半、只剩一人的合影。

abstract.en: Imagine a door marked out, with the room still full of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇标着「出」的门，房间里仍有光。

abstract.en: Think of a name with a small line drawn through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被画了一道小线的名字。

examples.en: She met her ex at a friend's wedding.
examples.cn: 她在朋友的婚礼上遇到了前任。

examples.en: He works with his ex-wife.
examples.cn: 他和前妻一起工作。

examples.en: My ex-boyfriend moved to another city.
examples.cn: 我的前男友搬到了另一座城市。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex」只有两个字母——像一个被划掉的名字前面的小叉，表示「以前的」。

root: 拉丁语 ex（出）→ 前缀 ex-（以前的）→ 口语名词 ex（前任）。

sensesIntro.en: Ex begins as a Latin word for out, becomes a prefix for former, and then stands alone to name a former partner.
sensesIntro.cn: ex 从拉丁语「出」开始，成为表示「以前的」前缀，最后单独指前任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a photo cut in half, leaving one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：被剪掉一半、只剩一人的合影。

branches.en: A former partner is the spoken noun.
branches.cn: 前任是口语中的名词用法。

branches.en: The prefix marks former status.
branches.cn: 前缀标记以前的身份。

branches.en: The abbreviation shortens example.
branches.cn: 缩写形式缩短 example。

branches.en: The noun grew out of the prefix.
branches.cn: 名词由前缀发展而来。

branches.en: Prefix and abbreviation both save space.
branches.cn: 前缀与缩写都在节省空间。

intro.en: Ex is both a Latin prefix and a small English word.
intro.cn: ex 既是拉丁前缀，也是一个简短的英语单词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ex, out of, is the source of the prefix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ex（出自）是前缀的来源。

items.exampleCN: ex 在口语中单独使用。

items.example: Ex-wife joins the prefix to wife.
items.exampleCN: ex-wife 把前缀与 wife 结合。
ex. 在印刷中缩短 example。

latinEntries.example: Ex is the source of the prefix.

definition_en: completely correct and precise
core_image: 一把刻度清晰到毫米的尺子
scene: 木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。The carpenter measured twice before drawing the exact cutting line on the board.
sceneCN: 这里 exact 是「精确的」（第 1 个义项：每个细节都完全正确）；句意：木匠量了两次，才在木板上画下精确的切割线。

senses.title: Completely correct
senses.definition: completely correct in every detail
senses.example: The exact time is ten past five.
senses.exampleCN: 确切时间是五点十分。
senses.why: Exact comes from Latin exigere, to weigh precisely.
senses.whyCN: exact 源自拉丁语 exigere（精确称量）。

senses.title: Strict
senses.definition: demanding great care and accuracy
senses.example: The exact rules must be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 必须遵守严格的规定。
senses.why: Precise measurement becomes strict demand.
senses.whyCN: 精确的衡量变成严格的要求。

senses.title: To demand
senses.definition: to demand and obtain something
senses.example: The teacher exacted an apology from the class.
senses.exampleCN: 老师要求全班道歉。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old sense of demanding payment.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了索取偿付的旧义。

intro.en: Exact comes from Latin exactus, past participle of exigere, to drive out or weigh.
intro.cn: exact 源自拉丁语 exactus，是 exigere（驱出、称量）的过去分词。

items.en: Agere means to drive or do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: Exigere means to drive out or weigh.
items.cn: exigere 意为驱出或称量。

items.en: Exactus means precise or exacted.
items.cn: exactus 意为精确的或被索取的。

items.en: Exact first describes precise measurement.
items.cn: exact 最初描述精确的测量。

items.en: It also means strict or demanding.
items.cn: 它也指严格或苛求的。

note.en: Exact stresses full correctness; precise stresses fine detail.
note.cn: exact 强调完全正确；precise 强调细节精细。

normalIntro.en: Exact is a ruler marked down to the smallest line.
normalIntro.cn: exact 是一把刻度细到最小格的尺子。

normal.en: Exact time means the precise hour and minute.
normal.cn: exact time 意为确切的小时和分钟。

normal.en: Exact words means the very words used.
normal.cn: exact words 意为原原本本的话。

normal.en: To be exact means to speak precisely.
normal.cn: to be exact 意为确切地说。

normal.en: An exact match fits perfectly.
normal.cn: an exact match 完全吻合。

normal.en: Compare precise: exact stresses no error, precise stresses fine detail.
normal.cn: 对比 precise：exact 强调无误差，precise 强调细节精细。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler with marks down to a millimeter.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻度细到毫米的尺子。

abstract.en: Imagine two puzzle pieces fitting without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图严丝合缝。

abstract.en: Think of a key that turns only in one lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一把只在一把锁里转动的钥匙。

examples.en: Can you give me the exact date?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我确切的日期吗？

examples.en: Those were his exact words.
examples.cn: 那就是他的原话。

examples.en: The work demands exact measurements.
examples.cn: 这项工作要求精确的测量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact」读起来短促干脆——像尺子一下卡到位，分毫不差。

root: 拉丁语 exigere（称量、要求）→ exactus（精确的）→ exact，核心义「量得准、要求严」。

sensesIntro.en: Exact starts with complete correctness, extends to strict demands, and keeps a verb sense of demanding.
sensesIntro.cn: exact 从完全正确开始，延伸到严格要求，还保留索取的动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler marked down to a millimeter.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度细到毫米的尺子。

branches.en: Complete correctness is the core.
branches.cn: 完全正确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision can become strictness.
branches.cn: 精确可以变成严格。

branches.en: The verb means to demand.
branches.cn: 动词意为强求。

branches.en: A measured standard and a strict rule meet.
branches.cn: 精确标准与严格规则相遇。

branches.en: Demanding payment and exact measuring share a root.
branches.cn: 索取与精确称量共享同一个词根。

intro.en: Exact joins ex-, out, to the Latin root ag, to drive.
intro.cn: exact 由 ex-（出）与拉丁词根 ag（驱动）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin exigere is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exigere 是直接来源。

definition_en: in a completely correct or precise way
core_image: 两块拼图严丝合缝地扣在一起
scene: 两块拼图恰好合上，边缘没有一点缝隙。The two puzzle pieces fit exactly, with no gap at the edge.
sceneCN: 这里 exactly 是「恰好、完全准确地」（第 2 个义项：正好合适）；句意：两块拼图恰好合上，边缘没有一点缝隙。

senses.title: Precisely
senses.definition: in a completely precise way
senses.example: Tell me exactly what happened.
senses.exampleCN: 把发生的事原原本本告诉我。
senses.why: The adverb describes an action done with full precision.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词描述以完全精确方式进行的动作。

senses.title: Just
senses.definition: used to stress that something is just right
senses.example: The train arrived exactly at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 火车正好在中午到达。
senses.why: Precision in time becomes the sense of just at.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的精确变成正好在。

senses.title: Absolutely
senses.definition: used to agree strongly
senses.example: That is exactly what I meant.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我的意思。
senses.why: Complete accuracy turns into strong agreement.
senses.whyCN: 完全的准确转成强烈赞同。

intro.en: Exactly is exact plus the adverb suffix -ly.
intro.cn: exactly 是 exact 加副词后缀 -ly。

items.en: Exactus means precise.
items.cn: exactus 意为精确的。

items.en: Exact describes what is correct.
items.cn: exact 描述正确的事物。

items.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 把形容词变成副词。

items.en: Exactly often marks a precise point in time.
items.cn: exactly 常标记确切的时间点。

items.en: It is also a strong way to agree.
items.cn: 它也是强烈赞同的说法。

note.en: Exactly points to full accuracy; precisely often sounds more formal.
note.cn: exactly 指向完全准确；precisely 往往更正式。

normalIntro.en: Exactly is the click of two pieces fitting together.
normalIntro.cn: exactly 是两块拼图扣合的那一声轻响。

normal.en: Exactly right means completely correct.
normal.cn: exactly right 意为完全正确。

normal.en: Exactly the same means no difference at all.
normal.cn: exactly the same 意为毫无差别。

normal.en: Not exactly means not completely.
normal.cn: not exactly 意为不完全是。

normal.en: Exactly at noon means at twelve sharp.
normal.cn: exactly at noon 意为正午整点。

normal.en: Compare precisely: precisely is more formal, exactly is more common in speech.
normal.cn: 对比 precisely：precisely 更正式，exactly 更常出现在口语中。

abstract.en: Picture two puzzle pieces locking without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两块拼图无缝扣合。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hand stops on the very mark.
abstract.cn: 想象钟的指针正停在刻度上。

abstract.en: Think of a word that lands on the center of a target.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词正中靶心。

examples.en: The two copies look exactly alike.
examples.cn: 两份副本看起来一模一样。

examples.en: That is exactly the answer I needed.
examples.cn: 那正是我需要的答案。

examples.en: She arrived exactly on time.
examples.cn: 她正好准时到达。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exact（精确的）＋ ly」——以精确的方式，就是确切地、恰好。

root: exact（精确的）＋ -ly（副词后缀）→ exactly，核心义「完全准确地」。

sensesIntro.en: Exactly marks full precision, stresses a point that is just right, and can express strong agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: exactly 标记完全精确，强调正好合适，也能表达强烈赞同。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two puzzle pieces locking without a gap.
core.cn: 核心意象：严丝合缝扣在一起的两块拼图。

branches.en: Full precision is the core.
branches.cn: 完全精确是核心含义。

branches.en: Precision in time becomes just at.
branches.cn: 时间上的精确变成正好在。

branches.en: Accuracy in words becomes agreement.
branches.cn: 语言上的准确变成赞同。

branches.en: A measure and a moment can both be exact.
branches.cn: 尺度与时刻都能精确。

branches.en: Time and agreement both land on the same point.
branches.cn: 时间与赞同都落在同一点上。

intro.en: Exactly is exact plus -ly.
intro.cn: exactly 是 exact 加 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The base exact comes from Latin exactus.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 exact 来自拉丁语 exactus。

definition_en: to describe something as bigger or better than it is
core_image: 一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋
scene: 他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。He always tends to exaggerate his experiences, turning a short trip into an adventure.
sceneCN: 这里 exaggerate 是「夸大」（第 1 个义项：把事情说得比实际更大）；句意：他总爱夸大自己的经历，把一次小旅行说成冒险。

senses.title: Making too much
senses.definition: to make something seem larger or better
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物显得更大或更好
senses.example: She exaggerated the size of the fish.
senses.exampleCN: 她夸大了那条鱼的大小。
senses.why: Ex- out and aggerare to pile up give the image of piling on.
senses.whyCN: ex-（出）与 aggerare（堆积）构成往上堆的意象。

senses.title: Overstating a feeling
senses.definition: to say something is stronger than it is
senses.example: He exaggerated his pain to get sympathy.
senses.exampleCN: 他为了博取同情夸大了疼痛。
senses.why: The same piling up applies to feelings.
senses.whyCN: 同样的堆积也适用于感受。

senses.title: To make too large
senses.definition: to make something larger than normal
senses.example: The wide lens exaggerates the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 广角镜头会夸大距离感。
senses.why: The visual sense keeps the literal idea of enlargement.
senses.whyCN: 视觉含义保留了放大的字面意思。

intro.en: Exaggerate comes from Latin exaggerare, to heap up.
intro.cn: exaggerate 源自拉丁语 exaggerare（堆高）。

items.en: Agger means a heap.
items.cn: agger 意为堆。

items.en: Aggerare means to heap up.
items.cn: aggerare 意为堆起。

items.en: Exaggerare means to pile up.
items.cn: exaggerare 意为堆积。

items.en: Exaggerate first means to heap up.
items.cn: exaggerate 最初意为堆高。

items.en: It means to overstate.
items.cn: 它逐渐指夸大其词。

note.en: Exaggerate is to describe too strongly; overstate is its formal twin.
note.cn: exaggerate 指描述得过头；overstate 是它更正式的同义词。

entries.definition: to make a number or claim seem larger

normalIntro.en: Exaggerate is piling extra words on a small fact.
normalIntro.cn: exaggerate 是在小事实上一层层堆词。

normal.en: Exaggerate the danger means make it seem worse.
normal.cn: exaggerate the danger 意为把危险说得更严重。

normal.en: Exaggerate the size means claim it is bigger.
normal.cn: exaggerate the size 意为声称尺寸更大。

normal.en: Grossly exaggerate means overstate very much.
normal.cn: grossly exaggerate 意为严重夸大。

normal.en: Without exaggerating means speaking plainly.
normal.cn: without exaggerating 意为毫不夸张地说。

normal.en: Compare overstate: exaggerate is everyday, overstate is formal.
normal.cn: 对比 overstate：exaggerate 更日常，overstate 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a small puddle drawn as a wide sea.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小水坑被画成一片汪洋。

abstract.en: Imagine a shadow at sunset stretching far beyond its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象日落时影子被拉得远远超过本人。

abstract.en: Think of a story that grows with every telling.
abstract.cn: 想象一个每讲一次就变大的故事。

examples.en: Don't exaggerate the difficulties.
examples.cn: 不要夸大困难。

examples.en: The report exaggerates the benefits of the plan.
examples.cn: 报告夸大了计划的好处。

examples.en: He tends to exaggerate when he is nervous.
examples.cn: 他紧张时容易夸大其词。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ agger（堆）」——往事实外面不断堆东西，就是夸大。

branches.en: Piling onto a fact is the core.

branches.en: Images can be enlarged as well.
branches.cn: 图像也能被放大。

intro.en: Exaggerate joins ex-, out, to the Latin root agger, a heap.

latinIntro.en: Latin exaggerare is the direct source.

definition_en: a formal test of knowledge or ability

senses.title: A test

senses.why: Exam is a short form of examination.

senses.title: A medical check

senses.why: The short form also covers medical checks.

senses.title: A formal assessment

senses.why: Exams can test skills, not only knowledge.

items.en: Examination names a formal test.

items.en: Exam shortens the long word.

abstract.en: Think of a door that opens only after a careful check.

examples.cn: 考试持续了两个小时。

examples.en: She studied hard for the final exam.
examples.cn: 她为期末考试努力学习。

root: 拉丁语 examen（天平指针，引申为检验）→ examination → exam。

branches.en: Any formal assessment counts.

branches.en: Knowledge and health are both examined.
branches.cn: 知识与健康都受到检验。

branches.en: Papers and driving tests share one name.
branches.cn: 试卷与驾照考试共用一个名称。

intro.en: Exam is a shortened form of examination.

latinIntro.en: Latin examen, a balance tongue, gives the root idea of testing.

definition_en: a formal test of knowledge, or a careful look at something
core_image: 考场上摊开的试卷和一支削好的铅笔
scene: 毕业考试的铃声响起，学生把准考证放在桌角。The final examination began as soon as the bell rang.
sceneCN: 这里 examination 是「考试」（第 1 个义项：对知识水平的正式测试）；句意：毕业考试的铃声响起，学生把准考证放在桌角。

senses.title: A formal test
senses.definition: a formal test of what someone knows
senses.definitionCN: 对某人知识水平的正式测试
senses.example: She passed the entrance examination.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过了入学考试。
senses.why: To examine someone's knowledge is to test it.
senses.whyCN: 考查某人的知识就是对其进行测试。

senses.title: A careful look
senses.definition: a close look at something to judge its state
senses.definitionCN: 为判断状况而仔细查看
senses.example: A medical examination found nothing wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 体检没有发现任何问题。
senses.why: The noun names the act of examining something closely.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指仔细检查某物的行为。

senses.title: A formal inquiry
senses.definition: an official process of asking questions
senses.example: The matter is still under examination.
senses.exampleCN: 此事仍在调查中。
senses.why: Questions put the facts on the scales.
senses.whyCN: 提问把事实放到天平上衡量。

intro.en: Examination comes from Latin examen, the tongue of a balance used for weighing.
intro.cn: examination 源自拉丁语 examen，即天平上用来称量的指针。

items.en: Examen means the tongue of a balance.
items.cn: examen 意为天平的指针。

items.en: Exigere, to weigh or drive out, is the source.
items.cn: exigere（称量、驱出）是其来源。

items.en: Old French examiner means to question closely.

items.en: English examination first means a careful inquiry.
items.cn: 英语 examination 最初指仔细调查。

items.en: It now also means a formal written test.
items.cn: 如今它也指正式的笔试。

note.en: Examination is the act or the test; examine is the verb behind it.

entries.definition: a short word for an examination

a set of questions to measure knowledge

normalIntro.en: Examination is the weighing of knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: examination 是对知识的一次称量。

normal.en: An exam is a shorter word for examination.
normal.cn: exam 是 examination 的简短说法。

normal.en: An examiner sets and marks the examination.
normal.cn: examiner 出题并批改 examination。

normal.en: A medical examination checks the body.
normal.cn: medical examination 检查身体。

normal.en: Under examination means being studied or checked.
normal.cn: under examination 意为正在被检查。

normal.en: Examination paper is the paper you write on.
normal.cn: examination paper 是你作答的试卷。

abstract.en: Picture a balance with knowledge on one pan.

abstract.en: Imagine a doctor reading a body like a map.
abstract.cn: 想象医生像读地图一样查看身体。

abstract.en: Think of a lamp shining into a dark box.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照进黑暗的盒子。

examples.en: The final examination lasts two hours.
examples.cn: 期末考试持续两小时。

examples.en: A close examination revealed a small crack.
examples.cn: 仔细检查发现了一条小裂缝。

examples.en: The plan is still under examination.
examples.cn: 该计划仍在审查中。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exam（考试）＋ ination」——把知识放到天平上称一称，就是考试与检查。

root: 拉丁语 examen（天平指针）→ 称量、考查 → 古法语 examiner → 英语 examination，核心义「把事物放上天平仔细称量」。

sensesIntro.en: Examination can be a formal test, a careful physical check, or an official inquiry.
sensesIntro.cn: examination 可以是正式考试、仔细检查，也可以是正式调查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: knowledge weighed on a balance.
core.cn: 核心意象：知识被放上天平称量。

branches.en: The formal test puts learning on the scales.
branches.cn: 正式考试把所学放上天平。

branches.en: A careful look weighs the state of things.
branches.cn: 仔细检查衡量事物的状况。

branches.en: Questions drive out the hidden facts.
branches.cn: 提问把隐藏的事实找出来。

branches.en: Both the test and the check begin with weighing.
branches.cn: 考试与检查都从称量开始。

branches.en: Inspection turns into inquiry when questions are asked.
branches.cn: 一旦开始提问，检查就变成调查。

intro.en: Examination builds on examine, from Latin examen, a balance tongue.

items.exampleCN: 该后缀把动词变成名词。

latinEntries.example: Examen is the root of examination.

definition_en: to look at something closely or test someone's knowledge

sceneCN: 这里 examine 是「检查」（第 1 个义项：仔细查看以了解状况）；句意：医院里，医生对着影像片仔细查看每一处细节。

senses.title: Looking closely
senses.definition: to look at something carefully to learn about it
senses.definitionCN: 仔细观察某物以了解情况

senses.why: The verb points a close look at one thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指向对某一事物的仔细查看。

senses.title: Testing knowledge
senses.definition: to test what someone knows

senses.exampleCN: 老师对全班进行了语法考试。
senses.why: Testing is a way of weighing knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 测试是称量知识的一种方式。

senses.title: Questioning formally
senses.definition: to question someone officially
senses.example: The police examined the witness for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 警方盘问了证人一小时。
senses.why: Questions dig out facts one by one.
senses.whyCN: 提问把事实一条条挖出来。

examples.cn: 出发前她仔细看了地图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ amine」——把问题一条条挖出来，就是检查与考查。

intro.en: Examine goes back to Latin exigere, to weigh or drive out.

definition_en: something that shows what a rule, group or person is like

definition_en: to be greater than a limit or to do better than others
core_image: 赛跑选手冲线时越过计分板上的旧纪录
scene: 马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。Her time exceeded the old record by two seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 exceed 是「超过」（第 1 个义项：在数量或程度上大于）；句意：马拉松终点前，一名选手越过了赛会保持多年的纪录。

senses.title: Being greater
senses.definition: to be more than a number or limit
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上大于某个数字或限度
senses.example: The cost exceeded our budget.
senses.exampleCN: 费用超出了我们的预算。
senses.why: The verb marks a step past a fixed line.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词标记跨过一条固定的线。

senses.title: Going beyond
senses.definition: to go past what is allowed
senses.example: He was fined for exceeding the speed limit.
senses.exampleCN: 他因超速被罚款。
senses.why: Crossing a limit is the same step, now against rules.
senses.whyCN: 越界是同一个动作，只是这次触犯了规则。

senses.title: Doing better
senses.definition: to do better than someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 表现得比某人或某物更好
senses.example: She exceeded all her rivals in the final round.
senses.exampleCN: 她在最后一轮中胜过了所有对手。
senses.why: Outrunning others is exceeding them.
senses.whyCN: 跑在别人前面就是胜过他们。

intro.en: Exceed comes from Latin excedere, to go out or go beyond.
intro.cn: exceed 源自拉丁语 excedere，意为走出、越过。

items.en: Cedere means to go or yield.
items.cn: cedere 意为走或让出。

items.en: Excedere joins ex-, out, with cedere, to go.
items.cn: excedere 由 ex-（出）与 cedere（走）组成。

items.en: Old French exceder keeps the sense of going beyond.
items.cn: 古法语 exceder 保留了越过的含义。

items.en: English exceed means to pass a limit.
items.cn: 英语 exceed 意为越过限度。

items.en: It now covers numbers, limits and rivals.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖数字、限度与对手。

note.en: Exceed is the verb; excess is the noun for too much.
note.cn: exceed 是动词，excess 是表示「过量」的名词。

entries.definition: an amount that is too much
to be better or greater than

normalIntro.en: To exceed is to step out past a line.
normalIntro.cn: exceed 就是跨出界线一步。

normal.en: Excess is the noun from exceed.
normal.cn: excess 是 exceed 对应的名词。

normal.en: Excessive means far too much.
normal.cn: excessive 意为过多。

normal.en: To exceed the limit is to cross it.
normal.cn: exceed the limit 就是越过界限。

normal.en: Sales exceeded expectations last year.
normal.cn: 去年销售额超出预期。

normal.en: Exceed and excess share the same root.
normal.cn: exceed 与 excess 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a runner's foot landing past the line.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者的脚落在终点线之外。

abstract.en: Imagine a glass filled beyond its rim.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子被倒得溢过杯口。

abstract.en: Think of an arrow flying past the target.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭飞过靶子。

examples.en: The bill exceeded what we had planned.
examples.cn: 账单超出了我们的计划。

examples.en: Demand for the tickets far exceeded supply.
examples.cn: 门票需求远远超过供给。

examples.en: He exceeded the speed limit on the highway.
examples.cn: 他在高速公路上超速了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex（出）＋ ceed（走）」——走出界限，就是超过。

root: 拉丁语 excedere（走出）＝ ex-（出）＋ cedere（走）→ 古法语 exceder → exceed，核心义「走出既定的界线」。

sensesIntro.en: Exceed means to be greater than a number, to pass an allowed limit, or to do better than others.
sensesIntro.cn: exceed 意为在数量上更大、越过允许的界限或胜过他人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot landing beyond the finish line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚落在终点线之外。

branches.en: Stepping past the line makes a number too large.
branches.cn: 跨过界线使数字变得过大。

branches.en: The same step breaks an allowed limit.
branches.cn: 同一个动作越过了允许的限度。

branches.en: Outrunning a rival is also exceeding.
branches.cn: 跑在对手前面也是 exceed。

branches.en: Numbers and rules both draw lines to pass.
branches.cn: 数字与规则都划出可被越过的线。

branches.en: Being greater and doing better share one image.
branches.cn: 数量更大与表现更好共用同一个意象。

intro.en: Exceed combines ex-, out, with Latin cedere, to go.
intro.cn: exceed 由 ex-（出）与拉丁语 cedere（走）组成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb excedere, to go out, passes through French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁动词 excedere（走出）经法语进入英语。

items.exampleCN: cedere 出现在 proceed 中。

items.example: Cede is the short English form.
items.exampleCN: cede 是简短的英语形式。

items.example: Exceed keeps the sense of stepping out.
items.exampleCN: exceed 保留了走出的含义。

items.example: Excess names the result of passing.
items.exampleCN: excess 指越过后产生的结果。

items.example: Proceed shares the same cedere root.
items.exampleCN: proceed 共享同一个 cedere 词根。

latinEntries.exampleCN: cedere 是 proceed 与 exceed 的基础。

latinEntries.example: Excedere is the source of exceed.
latinEntries.exampleCN: excedere 是 exceed 的来源。

definition_en: in an extreme degree; very
core_image: 暴雨夜里格外昏暗的巷口路灯
scene: 雨夜的巷子里，路灯显得格外昏暗。The alley was exceedingly dark in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 exceedingly 是「极其、格外」（第 1 个义项：达到极端的程度）；句意：雨夜的巷子里，路灯显得格外昏暗。

senses.title: To a very high degree
senses.definition: to an extremely high degree
senses.example: The task was exceedingly difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 这项任务极其困难。
senses.why: The adverb pushes an adjective to its extreme.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词推到极端。

senses.title: Beyond what is usual
senses.definition: more than is common or expected
senses.example: She was exceedingly patient with the child.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个孩子格外耐心。
senses.why: Going past the usual line makes a quality stand out.
senses.whyCN: 越过通常的界线，使某种特质格外突出。

senses.title: With great care
senses.definition: in a way that goes beyond the normal effort
senses.definitionCN: 以超出寻常努力的方式
senses.example: He prepared exceedingly well for the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 他为面试做了极为充分的准备。
senses.why: Effort that exceeds the norm shows in the manner.
senses.whyCN: 超出常规的努力会体现在方式上。

intro.en: Exceedingly adds -ly to exceeding, the participle of exceed.
intro.cn: exceedingly 由 exceed 的分词 exceeding 加 -ly 构成。

items.en: Excedere means to go beyond.
items.cn: excedere 意为越过。

items.en: Old French exceder carries the verb onward.
items.cn: 古法语 exceder 把动词继续传下去。

items.en: English exceed gives the participle exceeding.
items.cn: 英语 exceed 给出分词 exceeding。

items.en: The ending -ly turns it into an adverb.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把它变成副词。

items.en: Exceedingly now means extremely.
items.cn: 如今 exceedingly 意为极其。

note.en: Exceedingly strengthens a word; excessive describes too much of a thing.
note.cn: exceedingly 加强一个词，excessive 形容某物过多。

normalIntro.en: Exceedingly is exceeding plus -ly, pushing a word to its edge.
normalIntro.cn: exceedingly 是 exceeding 加 -ly，把一个词推到边缘。

normal.en: Exceedingly comes from exceeding.
normal.cn: exceedingly 来自 exceeding。

normal.en: It makes a strong word even stronger.
normal.cn: 它让原本强烈的词更强烈。

normal.en: Exceedingly rare means almost never seen.
normal.cn: exceedingly rare 意为几乎见不到。

normal.en: The -ly ending marks an adverb.
normal.cn: -ly 结尾标记副词。

normal.en: Avoid using it too often in speech.
normal.cn: 口语中不要过于频繁使用它。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer shooting past its top mark.
abstract.cn: 想象温度计冲过顶端的刻度。

abstract.en: Imagine a lamp so bright it hurts the eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏亮得刺眼的灯。

abstract.en: Think of a road that keeps climbing past the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象一条一直爬升到云层之上的路。

examples.en: The water was exceedingly cold.
examples.cn: 水极其寒冷。

examples.en: She is exceedingly careful with money.
examples.cn: 她花钱格外谨慎。

examples.en: The show was exceedingly popular.
examples.cn: 这场演出格外受欢迎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「exceeding（超过）＋ ly」——超过一般程度，就是极其、非常。

root: exceed（超过）→ exceeding（超出的）→ exceedingly（极其），核心义「超过一般程度地」。

sensesIntro.en: Exceedingly means to an extreme degree, beyond what is usual.
sensesIntro.cn: exceedingly 意为达到极端的程度，超出寻常。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer past its top mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：冲过顶端刻度的温度计。

branches.en: Going beyond the top mark is extreme.
branches.cn: 越过顶端刻度就是极端。

branches.en: Passing the usual line makes a quality stand out.
branches.cn: 越过通常的界线使特质格外突出。

branches.en: Great care shows in going beyond the norm.
branches.cn: 极为用心体现在超出常规。

branches.en: Extreme degree and unusual degree meet at the edge.
branches.cn: 极端程度与非常程度在边缘相遇。

branches.en: Both unusual quality and unusual effort exceed the norm.
branches.cn: 格外突出与格外用心都超出了常规。

intro.en: Exceedingly is exceed plus -ing and -ly.
intro.cn: exceedingly 由 exceed 加 -ing 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root cedere, to go, underlies the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 cedere（走）是这一词族的基础。

items.example: Cedere appears in exceed and proceed.
items.exampleCN: cedere 出现在 exceed 与 proceed 中。

items.example: The ending makes adverbs from adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成副词。
